name: Cabin Air Filter
summary: Second pass: the BMW MY2011 E90 owner's manual (p.105) says the car has a COMBINED microfilter / activated-charcoal filter that a BMW center replaces at routine maintenance, which closes the 'pollen vs carbon' question: the 2010 car should take the carbon element 64319313519 (now confirmed by Turner and Bimmerworld). The older pollen number 64316946628 is confirmed as the previous/superseded number (two bimmerpost threads plus Turner cross-reference). The filter housing is the long black plastic cover at the base of the windshield in front of the wipers (four sources). 8 mm socket is confirmed by four sources. Three retention tabs release the element (bavmods, single E90-E93 source). The manual also warns to rest the wiper arms against the windshield before opening the hood. Remaining open: fastener count is still a CONFLICT (3 on an E92 M3 write-up, 4 on bavmods E90-E93, 6 on a 2006 330i thread), because Bentley's procedure page is limited to cars built up to 12/2007 and the 2010 car's cover is not documented; airflow arrow direction for this car; torque (hand-snug only; no value); BMW replacement interval; and the CBS reset path is two-source but not confirmed on a 2010 car.
variantDependencies: Production date: Bentley's cover-removal video page is titled for E90/E91 produced up to 12/2007. A 2010 car (LCI) may have a different cover/housing and screw count; that page's content could not be read. Count conflicts (3/4/6) likely reflect this.

Filter type: MY2011 E90 manual p.105 says 'combined' microfilter / activated-charcoal filter replaced during routine maintenance; the part to buy is the carbon element (64319313519) unless the old filter shows otherwise.
Engine/transmission/drive: no source indicates any dependence.
Aftermarket cowl/delete kits exist (bavmods, acmtechnik) and change the procedure; check whether the car has one.

tools.item: Screwdriver or socket for the two duct screws (size unconfirmed)
tools.note: Poster says the two ducts attached to the cover have screws and two more pass through front tabs; size not stated beyond 8 mm.

parts.item: Genuine BMW activated-carbon cabin microfilter (combined microfilter/charcoal)
parts.note: Turner lists E90 328i N52 as Genuine BMW; Bimmerworld lists E90/E91/E92/E93 (06-13) 328i and the 2006-2011 E90 sedan, and links a replacement video; both advise replacing yearly or about every 15,000 miles (Bimmerworld) - not a BMW interval. The E90 manual p.105 describes the combined microfilter and charcoal layer.

parts.item: Pollen microfilter (older number; Turner shows it as a cross-reference of the carbon filter)
parts.note: Turner does not explicitly say superseded; it lists the number among previous revisions. Prefer the carbon number.

parts.item: Aftermarket carbon filters (Meyle PD for 64319313519; Mann/Hengst 64319142115)

torque.value: MISSING; tighten snugly by hand, plastic threads strip easily

steps.title: Prepare
steps.instruction: Engine off and cool. Before opening the hood make sure the wiper arms are resting against the windshield (BMW manual). Pull the hood release under the driver's side dashboard and open the hood.
warnings: Keep screws and debris out of the cowl drains and ducts beneath the cover.

steps.title: Locate the cover
steps.instruction: The cabin microfilter housing is the long black plastic cover along the base of the windshield in the engine bay, in front of the wipers, on the driver's side extending across the cowl.

steps.title: Remove the 8 mm fasteners
steps.instruction: Remove the 8 mm screws securing the cover and housing. Counts reported: three bolts (E92 M3, 2011), four screws (bavmods, E90-E93), six screws (2006 330i; two per duct plus two through front tabs). Remove all fasteners you find before lifting the cover, and count yours.
warnings: Plastic threads strip easily; do not over-tighten when refitting.
Remove all fasteners before lifting or the housing can break.
Do not drop screws into the cowl.

steps.title: Lift out the cover or filter assembly
steps.instruction: Lift the cover/assembly free of the cowl, noting how the ducts and any seals sit.

steps.title: Release and remove the old filter
steps.instruction: Depress the three retention tabs (bavmods) and pull the old filter out of its frame or cover. Note the way it sits: for BMW cabin filters the TIS rule quoted for a 2020 M550i is that the arrows point in the direction of airflow, but the E90 arrow direction was not found, so photograph the old filter before removing it.
warnings: Do not reinstall a dirty filter, and do not flip it; trapped dirt blows into the vents.

steps.title: Install the new filter
steps.instruction: Press the new activated-carbon filter fully into its frame so it sits flat and seals all around, matching the orientation of the old one.

steps.title: Reassemble
steps.instruction: Refit the cover and ducts, start all screws by hand, and tighten snugly. Check the cover seats flat and seals against the cowl.
warnings: Do not over-tighten the plastic threads.

steps.title: Reset the service reminder (optional)
steps.instruction: A 2011 bimmerpost reply: hold the trip-odometer reset button to enter the cluster menus, scroll with the left stalk to the fan / cabin-filter icon, then hold the BC button on the stalk to reset. FCP Euro's CBS guide (E90) uses the same hold-and-scroll method for other service items. Not confirmed for a 2010 car.

safety: Keep screws and debris out of the cowl drains and ducts.
Rest the wiper arms against the windshield before opening the hood (BMW manual) and work with the engine off and cool.
Do not drop fasteners or tools into the cowl; the covers underneath are hard to retrieve from.
missingEvidence: BMW/TIS/Bentley procedure for the cabin microfilter cover on a post-12/2007 E90 (Bentley page abstract is readable, steps and video are behind a login).
Fastener count and positions for a 2010 car (3, 4 and 6 reported).
Airflow arrow direction on the E90 filter.
BMW replacement interval for the microfilter (the manual says only 'routine maintenance'; retailers say yearly/15,000 miles).
Torque values (none exist in any source; hand-snug).
ownerInputsNeeded: Confirm the car has the factory cowl cover (not an aftermarket cowl-delete or filter kit).
Count the fastener screws on your cover and photograph the old filter's arrow/orientation before removing it.

visuals.title: Finding the cabin microfilter cover at the base of the windshield

elements.describe: A long black plastic cover running along the base of the windshield in the engine bay, in front of the wipers.
The 8 mm screws that hold the cover and its ducts; shown as screw heads without a specific count.
Wiper arms resting against the windshield above the cover, for orientation.
The lower edge of the windshield behind the cover.

Manual p.105 confirms a combined microfilter/charcoal filter exists; its engine-bay location text is not in the manual extract.
Bimmerpost: screws on the two ducts plus two through front tabs (six). bmwblog (E92 M3): two near the windshield and one closer to the front (three). Counts conflict; positions unresolved.
BMW manuals: have the wiper arms against the windshield before opening the engine compartment.
Bimmerpost (2 threads), bavmods and bmwblog all describe 8 mm screws on the cover/housing.
bimmerpost: on the two ducts and through front tabs; bmwblog: two near the windshield, one toward the front. Only a rough placement is supported.
